default.body: The solid hill is the accumulation of the dashed bump. Where the bump is tall, the hill steepens. Slide or grow the bump to reshape the hill.
default.title: Accumulation

default.body: Run right and watch the blue region grow. Each vertical strip you pass adds its height to the total area under the curve.
default.title: Area

default.body: The bars are the ridge z = f(x,0). Dashed level lines behind it are contours. Tighter contours mean a steeper climb.
default.title: The Contour Ridge

default.body: The V has two slopes. Skate each side, feel the kink at x = 0, then grab the a·f pad to steepen the whole V and reach the high shelf.
default.title: Corner

default.body: The S-curve y = x³/300 + 4 is steep, then flat, then steep again. The flat middle at x = 0 is the inflection, where concavity flips. Drift pushes you toward it; the tuning gem halves gravity for the steep right wall.
default.title: Inflection

default.body: Ride the exponential down toward a floor it never reaches. Each half-life halves the remaining distance. Collect ★ and the scale pad to feel the rate slow as the height shrinks.
default.title: Decay

knobDefs.label: Next Path
knobDefs.description: Page the clear overlay's Next button navigates to. Standalone default replays this world; riya-game-platformer overrides it with the next world's path.

default.body: The solid ramp is the slope of world 3's valley. The dashed ghost is the valley itself. Where the valley is flat, the ramp is near zero.
default.title: Derivative

default.body: The stairs follow y = 2^((x+8)/2): 1, 2, 4, 8. Grab the scale gems to double jump strength — apex grows like v², so double v quadruples height.
default.title: The Doubling Stair

default.body: A flat road y = 1 plus sine harmonics becomes a square-wave staircase. Grab harmonic pads to add terms, then ride the sum to every ★.
default.title: Fourier

knobDefs.label: Next Path
knobDefs.description: Page the clear overlay's Next button navigates to. Standalone default replays this world; riya-game-platformer overrides it with the next world's path.

default.body: The skyline is a Riemann sum. The shaded area grows as you move right. Pick the estimate that matches the shaded area at the gate.
default.title: The Gallery

default.body: The hill is z = 1 + 5·e^(−x²/18). Purple arrows are ∇f, pointing uphill. The hidden drift pulls you downhill.
default.title: Steepest Way Up

default.body: The graph y = 0.6x + 3 has a removable hole at x = 2. Approach from both sides; when the left and right heights agree, the road stitches itself.
default.title: The Limit

default.body: A logarithm bursts upward then flattens forever. The domain wall x = −7 is forbidden. Skate the curve, collect ★, then grab the phase pad to shift the graph and reach the far plateau.
default.title: Log

default.body: The hill has a summit. Climb until the slope flattens, grab +k to build a false peak, then reach every ★.
default.title: The Mountain

default.body: The plane z = 3 + x/4 + y/2 has two slopes. Walk the gentle x-direction; the dashed line is the steeper y-direction.
default.title: Two Slopes

default.body: Every spot on the ground is a number. Run right to make x bigger; gaps are missing numbers; the raised ledge is a larger value.
default.title: The Plain

knobDefs.label: Next Path
knobDefs.description: Page the clear overlay's Next button navigates to. Standalone default replays this world; riya-game-platformer overrides it with the next world's path.

default.body: A rational function has a vertical asymptote at x = 3. Skate the left branch, grab the tuning gem, and jump the discontinuity to the right branch.
default.title: The Pole

default.body: Each staircase is a line with its own slope. Skate the curves, collect ★, grab the ⚡ tuning pad to feel speed as slope.
default.title: The Ramp

default.body: The trail z = 2 + x²/12 dips to a minimum at x = 0. The cross-trail z = 4 − y²/6 peaks there. Same point, two behaviors.
default.title: The Mountain Pass

default.body: The yellow beacon slides toward x = 5 as you move right. The pink secant line connects you to the beacon; as the gap shrinks, its slope approaches the tangent slope.

default.body: Each step is half the previous: 1 + ½ + ¼ + … The staircase rises toward the ceiling S = 2 but never crosses it. Choose the limit to reach the final star.
default.title: Series

default.title: Shifts

knobDefs.description: Standalone default replays this world; riya-game-platformer overrides it with the next world's path.

default.body: The bars are the curve y = 1 + 12/(x+12). It creeps toward y = 1 but never touches it — yet the shaded area between them stays finite. Skate, collect ★, and grab the →1 pad.
default.title: Tail

knobDefs.description: When false the document look is a pure read surface: no header Edit button, no click-to-edit body, no click-to-rename title. knobDefs.label: Which field holds the document body?
knobDefs.description: Name of the field on the loaded record that carries the rich-text HTML body the document look renders and edits (e.g. content, body, articleText).
knobDefs.synonyms: body field, content field, document field

knobDefs.label: Which field is the cover image?
knobDefs.description: Name of the image-typed field on the loaded record painted as the document look's full-bleed hero banner (e.g. coverImage, heroImage). Empty = no banner, the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: cover field, hero image field, banner field

knobDefs.label: Detail look
knobDefs.description: Visual treatment for the record surface. panel = an inline detail-panel in the page flow (bodyContent); slide-over = the same panel as a right-hand drawer over the list behind it (slideOverBodyContent); page = a full-width record page with roomier spacing (pageBodyContent); document = a wiki-page/note/article surface — big editable title over a rich-text body, no labelled field rows, click-to-edit with autosave (documentBodyContent / documentEditingContent). Selecting a look swaps which body tree renders after the record loads; any body may still be overridden directly at the call site.
knobDefs.synonyms: detail style, drawer, slide over, full page, document, wiki page, note, article

knobDefs.label: Document look body (reading)
knobDefs.description: Render-ui SExpr for detailLook = document while reading: the pure writing surface — editable title with the rich-text body DIRECTLY beneath it, Edit and the actions menu tucked into the header corner. Metadata never sits between title and content; compose the sibling RecordItemDetails trait beside this one for the settings rail. Binds only @entity fields, never ?data, because it is also painted by arms whose payload is not the record.

knobDefs.label: Document look body (editing)
knobDefs.description: Render-ui SExpr for detailLook = document during an editing session: the same surface with the body live and the header corner showing the autosave hint + Done. Binds only @entity fields, never ?data.

knobDefs.label: Done button label
knobDefs.description: Label of the button that ends the document editing session; work is already autosaved when it is pressed.

knobDefs.label: Edit button label
knobDefs.description: Label of the quiet button above the document body that starts an editing session (the body itself is also clickable).

knobDefs.label: Which fields appear in the record panel?

knobDefs.synonyms: detail fields, record fields, panel fields, shown fields

knobDefs.label: Which field is the document icon?
knobDefs.description: Name of the field on the loaded record whose icon name renders beside the document title (e.g. icon). Empty = no icon, the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: icon field, glyph field

knobDefs.label: Which relation fields to hydrate?

knobDefs.label: How many actions before collapsing?

knobDefs.label: When does this surface load?

knobDefs.synonyms: open on click, slide over, row click, blank until opened, list embedded

knobDefs.label: Placeholder text

Empty = one ungrouped list, the default.

default.content:
أسسنا Almadar لمساعدة الشركات الناشئة والفرق الصغيرة على تحقيق ما تستطيع الشركات الكبيرة تحقيقه. بعد أكثر من 15 عامًا في بناء المنتجات الرقمية، ظللنا نرى نفس الشيء: فرق صغيرة متوقفة بسبب أدوات إما صلبة للغاية أو سحرية بزيادة عن اللزوم.

نؤمن أن البشر يجب أن يكونوا في قلب الثورة القادمة للذكاء الاصطناعي، وليس فكرة لاحقة. لهذا السبب Almadar Studio هو منشئ المنتجات للبشر أولاً، مع الذكاء الاصطناعي كمساعد.

نؤمن بشدة بالسيادة الرقمية. النماذج المفتوحة والبرمجيات مفتوحة المصدر هي الطريق إلى الأمام. Almadar Studio مبني على كود مفتوح المصدر بالكامل، وعملاؤنا ليسوا مقيدين بمزود. هدفنا تمكين الناس من بناء منتجات لا يحدها إلا خيالهم، ومنحهم الميزة التي يحتاجونها للتميز.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Section headline

default.content:
في Almadar، تصف منتجك مرة واحدة. ما يحتويه، القواعد التي تحكمه، ما يحدث عندما. هذا الوصف هو مصدر الحقيقة، ويبقى حيًا مع نمو منتجك.

كل شيء آخر يتدفق من هذا التعريف الواحد. المنتج يعمل منه ككود كامل يمكنك قراءته ونشره وامتلاكه. توثيقك يقرأ منه، لذا ما يراه فريقك في الويكي يتوافق دائمًا مع ما يعمل في الإنتاج. وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي يقرأون منه أيضًا، لذا يفهمون عملك بقراءة نفس ما يقرأه فريقك.

معظم الأدوات تولد الكود من توجيه وتنسى. Almadar يبقي التعريف في المركز، ويتيح لك تصديره أينما تحتاج: الكود، التوثيق، ووكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي الذين يعملون فوق عملك.

knobDefs.default: عرف منتجك مرة واحدة. استخدمه في كل مكان.

knobDefs.description: Section headline

default.content:
Almadar مفتوح المصدر من الأعلى إلى الأسفل. الأدوات التي تبني بها، والكود الذي نولده، والمنصة التي تشغلها كلها مفتوحة وقابلة للفحص. لا شيء يقيدك. لا شيء يحتجز بياناتك. لا عقد يمنعك من المغادرة.

أنت تمتلك الكود المولد. أنت تختار نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي. أنت تقرر أين يعمل. Almadar موجود ليمنح الفريق الصغير رافعة الفريق الكبير، لا ليجعلهم يعتمدون علينا.

default.content:
Almadar smo ustanovili, da bi pomagali zagonskim podjetjem in majhnim ekipam doseči to, kar lahko velika podjetja. Po več kot 15 letih gradnje digitalnih izdelkov smo vedno znova videli isto: majhne ekipe, zaustavljene z orodji, ki so bila bodisi preveč toga bodisi preveč čarobna, da bi jim zaupali.

Verjamemo, da morajo biti ljudje v središču prihajajoče revolucije umetne inteligence, ne pa pripomba za pozneje. Zato je Almadar Studio graditelj izdelkov, ki postavlja ljudi na prvo mesto, AI pa je pomočnik.

Močno verjamemo v digitalno suverenost. Odprti modeli in odprta koda sta pot naprej. Almadar Studio je zgrajen na popolnoma odprtokodni kodi in naši stranke nimajo zaklenitve ponudnika. Naš cilj je ljudem omogočiti gradnjo izdelkov, omejenih le z njihovo domišljijo, ter jim dati prednost, ki jo potrebujejo, da se izstopajo.

knobDefs.description: Section headline

default.content:
V Almadarju izdelek opišete enkrat. Kaj vsebuje, pravila, ki ga urejajo, kaj se zgodi, ko. Ta opis je vir resnice in ostaja živ, ko vaš izdelek raste.

Vse ostalo teče iz te ene definicije. Izdelek deluje iz nje kot celovita koda, ki jo lahko preberete, namestite in posedujete. Vaša dokumentacija jo bere, zato se to, kar vaša ekipa vidi v wikiju, vedno ujema s tem, kar teče v produkciji. AI agenti jo berejo tudi, zato razumejo vaše poslovanje, ker berejo isto kot vaša ekipa.

Večina orodij ustvari kodo iz poziva in pozabi. Almadar ohranja definicijo v središču in vam omogoča izvoz, kjer koli jo potrebujete: koda, dokumentacija in AI agenti, ki delujejo na vašem poslu.

knobDefs.default: Definiraj svoj izdelek enkrat. Uporabi ga povsod.

knobDefs.description: Section headline

default.content:
Almadar je odprtokoden od vrha do pete. Orodja, s katerimi gradite, koda, ki jo ustvarimo, in platforma, na kateri tečejo, so vsa odprta in pregledna. Nič vas ne zaklene. Nič ne drži vaših podatkov za talca. Nobena pogodba vas ne ustavi, da odidete.

Lastnik generirane kode ste vi. Izberete model AI. Odločite se, kje teče. Almadar obstaja, da bi majhni ekipi dal vzvod velike, ne da bi jo odvisno od nas.

knobDefs.label: Aggregation
knobDefs.description: How values within a bucket combine into one number
knobDefs.synonyms: user phrases: 'count' / 'how many' -> count; 'total' / 'sum of' -> sum; 'average' / 'mean' -> avg; 'minimum' / 'lowest' -> min; 'maximum' / 'highest' -> max

knobDefs.label: Group / categorize / bucket / split by field
knobDefs.description: Entity field whose values become the chart's category buckets. Set this when the user voices 'group by X' / 'categorize by X' / 'bucket by X' / 'split by X' / 'break down by X' for any non-time field X (for time-units, set period + timeAxis=true instead).
knobDefs.synonyms: regroup / rebucket / categorize / breakdown by / split by / segment by. user phrases: 'group by status' -> categoryField=status; 'group by region' / 'by region' -> categoryField=region; 'group by category' / 'by category' -> categoryField=category; 'group by product' / 'by product' -> categoryField=product; 'group by month' / 'by month' -> categoryField=month (when explicitly requested as a category, not a time bucket); 'split by X' / 'break down by X' / 'segment by X' / 'bucket by X' -> categoryField=X

knobDefs.label: Chart type
knobDefs.description: Visual format for the rendered chart
knobDefs.synonyms: bar = vertical bars, line = connected line, pie = pie chart, donut = pie with hole, area = filled area chart, histogram = frequency distribution, scatter = XY scatter. user phrases: 'switch to donut' / 'make it a donut' / 'as a donut chart' -> donut; 'use a pie chart' -> pie; 'show as line' / 'line chart' -> line; 'as bars' / 'bar chart' -> bar

knobDefs.label: Drill event
knobDefs.description: Event emitted when a user clicks a chart point
knobDefs.synonyms: click-through navigation event. user phrases: 'on click navigate to X' / 'drill into X' / 'when clicked open X' -> X event name

knobDefs.label: Chart height
knobDefs.description: Pixel height of the rendered chart
knobDefs.synonyms: vertical size in pixels. user phrases: 'taller' / 'make it taller' / 'increase height' / 'bigger vertically' -> larger number (e.g. 300, 400); 'shorter' / 'smaller' -> smaller; 'set height to 300' / '300px tall' -> 300

knobDefs.label: Top N
knobDefs.description: Keep only the first N points after sorting (0 = all)
knobDefs.synonyms: user phrases: 'top 5' -> 5; 'top 10' -> 10; 'first 3' -> 3; 'all' / 'no limit' -> 0; 'show all' -> 0

knobDefs.label: Group by month / quarter / week / day / year
knobDefs.description: Group by month, quarter, week, day, or year — the calendar bucket the chart groups data into. Set ALONGSIDE timeAxis=true whenever the user says 'group by <time-unit>' or 'by <time-unit>' or 'rebucket to <time-unit>' or 'instead of <other-time-unit>'.
knobDefs.synonyms: regroup / rebucket / change bucket / group differently. user phrases: 'group by month' / 'by month' / 'monthly' / 'monthly buckets' / 'switch to monthly' / 'instead of quarter' -> month; 'group by quarter' / 'by quarter' / 'quarterly' -> quarter; 'group by week' / 'by week' / 'weekly' / 'weekly buckets' -> week; 'group by day' / 'by day' / 'daily' / 'daily buckets' -> day; 'group by year' / 'by year' / 'yearly' / 'annually' -> year. Whenever the user voices 'group by <time-unit>' BOTH period AND timeAxis=true should be set.

knobDefs.label: Series
knobDefs.description: Pre-formatted multi-series spec for stacked or layered charts
knobDefs.synonyms: multiple lines / bars per category. user phrases: 'compare X and Y' -> add two series entries

knobDefs.label: Show legend
knobDefs.description: Display the series legend
knobDefs.synonyms: true shows the color key. user phrases: 'show legend' / 'show the legend' / 'show key' / 'with legend' / 'with a legend' -> true; 'hide legend' / 'no legend' / 'without legend' / 'remove legend' -> false

knobDefs.label: Show values
knobDefs.description: Render the numeric value on top of each data point
knobDefs.synonyms: user phrases: 'show values' / 'show numbers on bars' / 'with data labels' / 'label the bars' -> true; 'hide values' / 'no labels' -> false

knobDefs.label: Sort direction
knobDefs.description: Ascending or descending order for the sort field
knobDefs.synonyms: asc = ascending = lowest-to-highest = low-to-high = smallest-first. desc = descending = highest-to-lowest = high-to-low = largest-first. user phrases: 'highest to lowest' / 'largest first' / 'descending' -> desc; 'lowest to highest' / 'smallest first' / 'ascending' -> asc

knobDefs.label: Sort by
knobDefs.description: Order points by value, label, or leave unsorted
knobDefs.synonyms: user phrases: 'sort by value' / 'order by amount' -> value; 'sort alphabetically' / 'sort by name' -> label; 'no sort' / 'leave order' -> none

knobDefs.label: Stacking
knobDefs.description: Stack bars, normalize to 100%, or render side-by-side
knobDefs.synonyms: user phrases: 'side by side' / 'grouped' -> none; 'stacked' / 'stack the bars' -> stack; 'percent stacked' / '100% stacked' / 'normalized' -> normalize

knobDefs.label: Subtitle
knobDefs.description: Secondary line below the title
knobDefs.synonyms: secondary header below the title. user phrases: 'with subtitle X' / 'set subtitle to X' -> X

knobDefs.label: Time axis
knobDefs.description: Group by timeField bucketed by period instead of categoryField
knobDefs.synonyms: true means group by date / month / time. user phrases: 'group by month / week / year / date' -> set timeAxis=true; 'group by status / category' -> timeAxis=false

knobDefs.label: Date field
knobDefs.description: Entity field used as the time axis when timeAxis is on
knobDefs.synonyms: the date / timestamp / created-at column. set when timeAxis=true

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the chart
knobDefs.synonyms: the chart's header text. user phrases: 'rename to X' / 'title it X' / 'change the title to X' / 'call it X' -> X

knobDefs.label: Value field
knobDefs.description: Numeric field aggregated per bucket (blank = row count)
knobDefs.synonyms: the numeric column to aggregate. empty string counts rows. user phrases: 'sum revenue' -> valueField=revenue + aggregation=sum

knobDefs.label: Render pattern
knobDefs.description: UI pattern used to draw the chart
knobDefs.synonyms: internal pattern selector. user prompts rarely target this directly — pattern selection is upstream

knobDefs.description: Subject line used for the email channel. Falls back to `template` when blank. Ignored for other channels.
knobDefs.synonyms: subject, subject line, email title, mail subject

knobDefs.label: Event key for preferences
knobDefs.description: Stable key naming the upstream event this listener is bound to (e.g. 'OrderPlaced'). NotificationPreference rows (std-notification-center) whose eventType equals this key — or is blank — apply to this listener's dispatches.
knobDefs.synonyms: preference key, event name, subscription key, notification topic

knobDefs.label: Fallback recipient
knobDefs.description: Recipient used when `recipients` is empty, instead of the acting user. The acting-user fallback (used when this is blank) is intended for personal notifications only — set this to an ops/team address (e.g. 'ops@example.com') for system alerts like low-stock or shipping notices, so the acting user isn't notified in place of the intended audience.
knobDefs.synonyms: default recipient, backup recipient, ops address, fallback address, notify default, alert owner

knobDefs.label: Frequency cap (per week)
knobDefs.description: Max dispatched sends per (channel, recipient) per rolling 7-day window, counted against dispatched NotificationRecord audit rows. 0 = uncapped. Applies to the persisted channels (email/sms/push/webhook); in-app toasts are not audited and not capped. A capped dispatch persists an audit row (`error: frequency-cap`, dispatched:false).
knobDefs.synonyms: rate limit, cap, max per week, throttle, send limit

knobDefs.label: Guard field (numeric)
knobDefs.description: Field read from the upstream event's `data` payload and compared against `guardValue` when `guardOp` is not `eq` (e.g. 'stockLevel', 'quantity'). Ignored when `guardOp` is `eq`.
knobDefs.synonyms: threshold field, numeric field, compare field, watched field, data field

knobDefs.label: Guard comparison
knobDefs.description: How to gate dispatch. `eq` (default) does string-equality via `triggerStatus` against the upstream event's `status` field, exactly as before. `gt`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte` instead numerically compare `guardField` (read from the event's `data` payload) against `guardValue` — e.g. fire only when a stock level drops below a threshold.
knobDefs.synonyms: comparison operator, threshold operator, guard mode, trigger comparison, numeric gate, greater than, less than, threshold crossing

knobDefs.label: Guard value (numeric)
knobDefs.description: Threshold compared against `guardField` when `guardOp` is not `eq` (e.g. fire when stock drops below 5).
knobDefs.synonyms: threshold, cutoff, limit, watermark, trigger value

knobDefs.label: Trigger events
knobDefs.description: Event names that should fire a notification. Set this to the upstream event name (e.g. OrderPlaced, CheckoutCompleted) so this atom listens for events from the orbital that emits them. The orbital owning this trait reacts whenever the named event fires anywhere in the schema.
knobDefs.synonyms: subscribe to event, listen for event, react to event, watch for, wire upstream event, observe event from another orbital, cross-orbital subscription, on-event trigger

knobDefs.label: Channel
knobDefs.description: Delivery channel. `in-app` (default) emits the in-app `notify` toast. `email`/`sms`/`webhook` dispatch through call-service at event time (email.send / twilio.sendSMS / webhook.send) and persist a NotificationRecord audit row with an honest `dispatched` flag: true only once the service call succeeds, false plus the failure detail in `error` otherwise. `push` looks up the recipient's PushSubscription row (captured by std-notification-center's subscribe flow) and dispatches web-push via push.send — a recipient with no subscription records the audit row undispatched (`no-push-subscription`). `webhook` requires `webhookUrl` to actually dispatch; a blank `webhookUrl` still records the audit row undispatched rather than failing. A per-user NotificationPreference row with a non-blank `channel` overrides this value for that recipient.
knobDefs.synonyms: delivery method, notification channel, send via, dispatch through, push notification, web push

knobDefs.label: Push deep link
knobDefs.description: In-app path opened when the recipient clicks the push notification (e.g. '/orders'). Blank = the app root.
knobDefs.synonyms: click url, open on click, target path, notification link

knobDefs.label: Push icon
knobDefs.description: Icon URL shown on the push notification. Blank = the browser default.
knobDefs.synonyms: notification icon, badge image

knobDefs.label: Push title
knobDefs.description: Notification title for the push channel. Falls back to `template` when blank. Ignored for other channels.
knobDefs.synonyms: notification title, push heading, alert title

knobDefs.label: Quiet hours end
knobDefs.description: Hour of day (0-23) when the atom-level quiet window closes. Equal to `quietStartHour` = disabled.
knobDefs.synonyms: do not disturb until, silence end, night mode end

knobDefs.label: Quiet hours start
knobDefs.description: Hour of day (0-23) when the atom-level quiet window opens. Equal to `quietEndHour` = disabled. Dispatches inside the window persist an audit row (`error: quiet-hours`, dispatched:false) which std-notification-center's digest cycle drains later. Per-user quiet hours from NotificationPreference rows apply in addition.
knobDefs.synonyms: quiet hours, do not disturb from, silence start, night mode start

knobDefs.label: Recipients
knobDefs.description: Recipient ids/addresses. v1.1 uses the first entry; multi-recipient fan-out lands in v1.2 (gap). When empty, falls back to `fallbackRecipient` if set, otherwise the authenticated user.
knobDefs.synonyms: targets, addressees, notify to

knobDefs.label: Severity
knobDefs.description: info, success, warning, or error — controls styling
knobDefs.synonyms: alert level, priority, urgency

knobDefs.label: Suppression list
knobDefs.description: Recipient ids/addresses to skip (e.g. unsubscribed users). Suppression check runs before dispatch.
knobDefs.synonyms: block list, unsubscribed, opt-out list

knobDefs.label: Message template
knobDefs.description: Text shown to the recipient; supports payload interpolation
knobDefs.synonyms: notification text, message body, alert text

knobDefs.label: Trigger status
knobDefs.description: When `guardOp` is `eq` and this is set, dispatch only when the upstream event's `status` field equals this value (e.g. fire only when a record becomes 'approved'). Empty = fire on every subscribed event. Ignored when `guardOp` is a numeric comparison.
knobDefs.synonyms: on status, when status, status filter, only when, fire on, react on status

knobDefs.label: Webhook secret
knobDefs.description: Signing secret forwarded to the webhook service so the receiving endpoint can verify the payload. Ignored when `webhookUrl` is blank.
knobDefs.synonyms: signing secret, hmac secret, webhook signature, shared secret

knobDefs.label: Webhook URL
knobDefs.description: Destination endpoint for the webhook channel. Dispatch only fires when this is non-blank; a blank URL on channel "webhook" records the audit row with dispatched:false instead of crashing (a consumer misconfiguration, not a failure).
knobDefs.synonyms: webhook endpoint, callback url, target url, http endpoint, notify url

knobDefs.label: Burst size
knobDefs.description: Requests allowed to burst above the per-minute rate before steady-state throttling kicks in. Lower burst = strict/no-spikes; higher burst = forgiving/allow-spikes.
knobDefs.synonyms: burst capacity, allowance, spike allowance, no-spike (low) vs allow-bursts (high)

knobDefs.label: Enabled
knobDefs.description: Whether rate limiting is active for the host orbital. Off by default; turn on to throttle requests.
knobDefs.synonyms: enable, turn on, enforce, require, activate, apply, switch on, rate limit, throttle, requests per minute, slow down, cap usage, request cap, limit traffic, prevent abuse

knobDefs.label: Rate-limit key strategy
knobDefs.description: What identifier the per-bucket counter is keyed on: source IP, authenticated user, API key, or one global bucket.
knobDefs.synonyms: limiter key, bucket key

knobDefs.label: Override roles
knobDefs.description: Roles exempt from rate limiting (e.g. internal services, admin override). Empty = no exemptions.
knobDefs.synonyms: exempt roles, bypass list

knobDefs.label: Requests per minute
knobDefs.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute before throttling begins.
knobDefs.synonyms: rate limit, request cap, RPS, throttle threshold

knobDefs.label: Anonymize on rejection
knobDefs.description: When true, scrub PII (name, email, phone, resumeUrl) on REJECT_APPLICANT. Pair with std-data-erasure.

knobDefs.label: E-Verify required

knobDefs.description: Revision entity field holding the parent document's id. knobDefs.label: Export event
knobDefs.description: Event emitted when the user picks a format. Each entry in formats[] carries its own literal event field (no per-item templating in .lolo) — overriding this alone does not retarget the click; also set formats[].event to match.

knobDefs.label: Available formats
knobDefs.description: Export formats shown to the user in the popover
knobDefs.synonyms: list of export format entries (csv / xlsx / pdf / png / json). user phrases: 'only CSV' -> keep only csv entry; 'add JSON' -> append json entry; 'no PNG' -> remove png; 'allow X and Y' -> set the array to those two

knobDefs.label: Tile id
knobDefs.description: Identifier of the dashboard tile being exported
knobDefs.synonyms: internal identifier — host orbital wires this; users rarely set it directly

knobDefs.label: Button label
knobDefs.description: Text shown on the toolbar button that opens the import source popover
knobDefs.synonyms: the text on the import trigger button. user phrases: 'rename import button to X' / 'set the button label to X' -> X (e.g. 'Import Data', 'Add Sources')

knobDefs.label: Source-picked event
knobDefs.description: Event emitted when the user picks a source. Each entry in sources[] carries its own literal event field (no per-item templating in .lolo) — overriding this alone does not retarget the click; also set sources[].event to match.
knobDefs.synonyms: bus event name. internal wiring; users rarely target directly

knobDefs.label: Import sources
knobDefs.description: Sources shown in the import popover. kind 'file' opens the OS file picker before IMPORT_REQUESTED; any other kind emits immediately (the host renders the matching input UI, e.g. a paste textarea).
knobDefs.synonyms: list of import source entries (paste / file / api / database). user phrases: 'only paste' -> keep only the paste entry; 'add database' -> append a database entry

knobDefs.label: Import storage key
knobDefs.description: Object-storage key of a previously stored schema to load on import. Blank keeps import as clipboard-only paste (today's behavior, unchanged). When set together with storageBucket, picking Import downloads this key's content and stages it in the editor instead of reading the clipboard.
knobDefs.synonyms: import key, stored schema key, storage object key

knobDefs.label: Export/import storage bucket
knobDefs.description: Object-storage bucket for durable schema export/import. Blank keeps export as a clipboard-only copy and import as clipboard-only paste (today's behavior, unchanged). Set it to upload exports for a real signed download link and, together with importKey, to download a stored schema on import.
knobDefs.synonyms: storage bucket, schema bucket, export bucket

knobDefs.label: Categories
knobDefs.description: The two-way classification ladder: allophones of one phoneme (complementary distribution, no meaning contrast) versus separate phonemes (a minimal pair contrasts meaning in an identical environment).
knobDefs.synonyms: phoneme, allophone, complementary distribution, minimal pair, contrast, phonology

default.explanation: A minimal pair (sip/zip) proves [s] and [z] contrast in identical environments and change meaning — they are separate phonemes /s/ and /z/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final. Features — [s]: +consonantal, −voice, +coronal, +strident. [z]: +consonantal, +voice, +coronal, +strident.
default.text:
English [s] and [z] — are [s] and [z] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- sip [sɪp]  vs  zip [zɪp] — same environment, meaning changes
- seal [siːl]  vs  zeal [ziːl] — same environment, meaning changes
- A minimal pair exists: swapping [s] for [z] makes a different word.

default.explanation: Clear [l] and dark [ɫ] stand in complementary distribution — [l] in onsets, [ɫ] in codas — so they are allophones of one phoneme /l/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final. Features — [l]: +consonantal, +voice, +lateral, −velarized. [ɫ]: +consonantal, +voice, +lateral, +velarized.
default.text:
English clear [l] and dark [ɫ] — are [l] and [ɫ] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- leaf [liːf] — clear [l] only before a vowel
- feel [fiːɫ] — dark [ɫ] only word-finally after a vowel
- No minimal pair exists: the two sounds never occur in the same environment.

default.explanation: Stop [d] appears after pauses and nasals, fricative [ð] between vowels — complementary distribution makes them allophones of /d/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final.
default.text:
Spanish [d] and [ð] — are [d] and [ð] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- donde [donda] — [d] after a nasal
- nada [naða] — [ð] between vowels
- No minimal pair exists: each sound is tied to its own phonological environment.

knobDefs.description: Color of the retention curve and its current-value marker.

knobDefs.label: Decay Rate
knobDefs.description: Exponential forgetting rate — each STEP_TIME multiplies retention by exp(−decayRate · Δt).

knobDefs.label: Grid Step
knobDefs.description: Spacing between gridlines on the canvas, in time units.

knobDefs.label: Reference Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the no-repetition reference decay curve.

knobDefs.label: Repetition Boost
knobDefs.description: Fraction of the forgotten gap (1 − retention) recovered by one repetition; the massed preset halves it to model cramming's weaker encoding.
knobDefs.synonyms: repetition effect, rehearsal boost, spacing effect, relearning savings

knobDefs.label: Schedule Preset
knobDefs.description: Practice schedule being demonstrated: massed practice (cramming) recovers only half the boost per repetition, spaced practice recovers the full boost — the spacing effect.
knobDefs.synonyms: spaced repetition, distributed practice, massed practice, cramming, spacing effect

knobDefs.label: Time Horizon
knobDefs.description: Total time units shown on the x-axis; each STEP_TIME advances one twentieth of it.

knobDefs.label: Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the cumulative-response curve.

knobDefs.label: Grid Step
knobDefs.description: Spacing between gridlines on the canvas.

knobDefs.description: Time units required per reinforcer on interval schedules; VI alternates between intervalLength ± half.
knobDefs.synonyms: interval requirement, fixed interval length, inter-reinforcement interval

knobDefs.label: Ratio N
knobDefs.description: Responses required per reinforcer on ratio schedules; VR alternates between ratioN ± half.
knobDefs.synonyms: ratio requirement, fixed ratio size, response requirement

knobDefs.label: Reinforcer Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the reinforcement markers on the cumulative record.

knobDefs.label: Response Cap
knobDefs.description: Y-axis maximum of the cumulative record, in cumulative responses.

knobDefs.label: Response Rate

knobDefs.label: Time Cap

knobDefs.description: Probability that a simulated trial actually contains a signal — governs the empirical hit/false-alarm mix in RUN_TRIALS.
knobDefs.synonyms: base rate, signal prevalence, prior probability, signal probability

knobDefs.label: Criterion
knobDefs.description: Initial decision threshold on the evidence axis; evidence above it triggers a 'signal present' response. Hit rate is Φ(d′ − c), false-alarm rate Φ(−c).
knobDefs.synonyms: decision criterion, response bias, threshold, beta, cutoff

knobDefs.label: Criterion Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the criterion line and marker.

knobDefs.label: d′ (Sensitivity)
knobDefs.description: Separation between the noise and signal+noise distributions, in standard deviations — the learner's sensitivity to the signal.
knobDefs.synonyms: d prime, sensitivity, discriminability, signal strength, detectability

knobDefs.label: Noise Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the noise distribution curve.

knobDefs.label: Signal Curve Color

knobDefs.label: Which field does the first load filter on?
knobDefs.description: Name the field the INITIAL load filters on, paired with initialFilterValue. This is the detail half of a list-detail pair: a thread that must wait for a conversation to be picked sets the field to its parent key and leaves the value blank, so the first load matches nothing and the empty state shows instead of every record in the table. REFETCH_FILTER then supplies the real selection. Left blank the first load is unfiltered, which is the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter, first load filter, wait for selection, detail pane filter, requires selection, start empty

knobDefs.label: What value does the first load filter for?
knobDefs.description: The value initialFilterField must equal on the first load. Blank is meaningful: it matches only records whose field is itself blank, which for a detail pane is normally none — that is how a thread stays empty until its parent is selected.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter value, first load value, default selection

default.explanation: Lemert's primary deviance: a norm was violated and mildly sanctioned, but no deviant label was applied or internalized — the act passes without reshaping anyone's identity or status.

options.label: Conforming — no norm was really broken.
Primary deviance — norm violation, minor informal sanction, no label.
Secondary deviance — a formal label was internalized.

default.text: A driver is ticketed for speeding, pays the fine, and thinks no more of it; neither does anyone else.

default.explanation: Secondary deviance (Lemert): once the formal label is applied by the justice system and internalized, the deviant identity organizes further behavior — deviance amplified by the societal reaction itself, the core claim of labeling theory.

options.label: Primary deviance — the label never stuck.
Conforming — he was only adjusting to expectations.
Secondary deviance — the formal label was applied and internalized, organizing further deviance.

default.text: A teenager caught shoplifting is arrested, formally charged, and comes to be treated — and to see himself — as a 'delinquent'; he re-offends.

default.explanation: Primary deviance: a minor norm violation that draws no sanction and no label. Most people commit such acts occasionally without any consequence for their identity — deviance is common; being labeled deviant is rare.

options.label: Primary deviance — a minor violation with no sanction and no label.
Secondary deviance — the label reshapes her identity.
Conforming — taking office supplies is fully normative.

default.text: An office worker takes a pen home from the supply closet; everyone does it, nobody comments, and it is never punished.

default.explanation: Conforming: the act follows the governing norms (policy and professional ethics) rather than violating them. That the supervisor disliked it does not make it deviant — deviance is defined against the group's norms, not a superior's preference.

options.label: Primary deviance — refusing a superior is always a violation.
Conforming — the act follows the governing norms and is rewarded.
Secondary deviance — the commendation is a label.

default.text: A nurse refuses an unsafe order from a supervisor because hospital policy and professional ethics forbid it, and is formally commended.
